name: יִמְלָה
summary: Imlah, father of Micaiah, the prophet of Yahweh whom Ahab hated because he prophesied evil and not good concerning him, and who foretold Ahab's death at Ramoth-gilead (1Ki 22:8–28; 2Ch 18). He is named only as Micaiah's father. Kings spells the name יִמְלָה and Chronicles יִמְלָא, which is the qal imperfect of מָלֵא, “he fills” or “he will fill”; the ending ה for א is found in the same root in Job 8:21, יְמַלֵּה “he will fill”. Many Hebrew names are a verb in the imperfect with God the unspoken subject (יִצְחָק, “he laughs”), so the name likely means “(God) fills”, perhaps of filling the house with a son, but scripture does not explain it.

evidence.note: “There is yet one man by whom we may inquire of Yahweh, Micaiah the son of יִמְלָה, but I hate him, for he does not prophesy good concerning me, but evil.”
The same words, with the name spelt יִמְלָא: the qal imperfect of מָלֵא.
“He will yet fill (יְמַלֵּה) your mouth with laughter”: a form of מָלֵא written with final ה for א, as in יִמְלָה.
Sarah: “God has made laughter for me”, the explanation of יִצְחָק, a name that is a verb in the imperfect.
Micaiah: “If you return in peace at all, Yahweh has not spoken by me.”

note: Scripture gives no explanation of the name; the reading “he fills” rests on the Chronicles spelling יִמְלָא and the ה/א variation shown in Job 8:21. BDB's j.bq.af (יִמְלָה, zero tokens) is a cross-reference to m.bz.ai and is not listed.
